rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential read of chunks 0-4 turns up no unresolved referent. Chunk 3 header 'You just ran the same loop' (line 25) introduces 'loop' and the same sentence-group resolves it in-chunk ('This build story is the shape you just ran'); chunk 4 header 'What compounds' (line 31) reuses 'compound engineering' named one slide earlier at line 29 ('Kieran Klaassen calls this **compound engineering**') — a term introduced on an earlier slide and reused, explicitly not a violation. Chunk 4's closer 'The loop is the shape' (line 42) calls back to the same chunk-3 vocabulary, one slide back, same file — allowed. Session-artifact carve-out applies to 'the rules file you just wrote' (chunk 2, line 23) and 'the file you wrote today' (chunk 4, line 40): verified against the module's include order in curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md (lines 50/52/54) that compound-and-close.md (Ex4, 'write your rules file' / './CLAUDE.local.md') runs immediately before this lecture in M1 — the referent is the student's lived module, per the carve-out. Harm (a reader losing the thread) is absent throughout.

grep -n for any 'the opening lecture said' / positional-callback shape across the body (lines 1-43) returns nothing. The closest candidate is chunk 2 line 21, 'Modules 1-6' inside 'a tmux runner drives real Claude Code sessions through Modules 1-6 against working codebases' — this names a technical test-coverage fact about the QA tooling (matches the backing block's tmux-runner source stamp), not a positional pointer at another file or a pedagogical map reveal to the student; it stays inside. No in-body link exists to check for un-named-document phrasing (confirmed under rule 13).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two backward references checked against the live module: 'the rules file you just wrote' (chunk 2, line 23) and 'wrote what the session taught you into ./CLAUDE.local.md' (chunk 3, line 27). Ran: grep -n 'CLAUDE.local.md|rules file|## ' curriculum/exercises/compound-and-close.md -> confirms '## Write your rules file from the session' (line 17) and 'The rules land in ./CLAUDE.local.md' (line 13). Module include order (getting-going.md lines 50/52/54) places compound-and-close before this lecture in M1. Both beats exist and precede this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess/predict-before-reveal instruction anywhere in the body (grep for 'guess'/'predict' returns nothing) — this is a narrative story lecture with no live-demo beat for the rule to check.

All four ## chunks carry multi-sentence, self-carrying content (chunk 1: 186 words per check-slide-size.js --report; chunk 2: 154 words; chunk 3: 57 words but a complete claim+payoff; chunk 4: 121 words / 4 bullets). None is a single context-dependent wait-state bullet.

Checked each header against its chunk body: 'Everything starts as a few bulletpoints somewhere' (line 5) is echoed by the first sentence 'At first, this training was a strategy document: seven headings and thirty bulletpoints' (line 7) — true. 'Then we tested the training' (line 15) is carried by the judges/simulation/tmux content that follows — true. 'You just ran the same loop' (line 25) is carried by 'This build story is the shape you just ran on your own repo' (line 27) — true. 'What compounds' (line 31) is carried by Klaassen's definition and the four bullets that follow — true, no header is contradicted by its own content.

Checked each sub-item across all four chunks. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction: grep -n '. Not ' over lines 1-43 returns nothing. Anaphora/epistrophe triples: closest candidate is chunk 1 line 11 'Some were too broad. Some fired in the wrong place' — a PAIR, not a triple, explicitly not the banned shape. Self-grading superlatives: none found (no 'one of the most...' or equivalent). Number + own retraction: closest candidate is chunk 1 line 13 '302 active rules and subrules across 12 checklists, written over 1,447 commits. Neither count is a claim that more rules make better work' — this is not the banned hedge-the-measurement tic (the number is stated with full confidence and mechanically verified per the backing block's compendium-snapshot stamp); it is a distinct move, a caution against a specific misreading (more rules != better work), and the maintainer's own Watch-fors block (line 74) REQUIRES this exact sentence ('The rule count reads as a quality score. The following sentence must keep explaining what the count does and does not show') — deliberate, not a tic. Abstraction-noun stacks: none found. Verb triplets with an empty leg: none found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No occurrence of compendium/surface-as-noun/beat/mood/Connections-as-proper-noun in the body. Two near-misses checked and cleared: (1) chunk 1 line 9, 'Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go' — verbatim check_pedagogy.md §16, quoted as a specimen (the correction-to-rule move made concrete), covered by the compendium's own 'maintainer rule quoted as a specimen' exception and by the maintainer block's own note at line 55 naming this exact quote; displayed, not used as vocabulary. (2) chunk 1 line 11, 'Some fired in the wrong place' — 'fired' here is ordinary rule-engine/trigger vocabulary (a rule 'fires'), not the repo-specific coinages the rule targets (compendium, surface-as-noun); applying the rule's own register test ('weigh audience register... genuinely repo-internal' vs 'ordinary shop vocabulary'), an AE101 engineer IC parses 'fired' without translation. 'tmux' (chunk 2, line 21) is a real external tool name, pre-cleared by the maintainer's Register check block (line 79: 'Engineer-audience terms (tmux, automated quality judges, prompt behavior) are used only where their mechanics add value').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -no for '**...**' spans across the whole body (lines 1-43) returns exactly one hit: line 29, '**compound engineering**' (2 words, a coined-term handle, inside chunk 3). Zero bold in chunks 0, 1, 2, and 4 (including the new 'What compounds' slide's four bullets and closer). Matches the maintainer's own standing constraint at line 49: 'Narrative slides stay prose paragraphs. The only bold student-side handle is **compound engineering**.' Well within the <=1-per-slide, <=5-word handle cap.

rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is a named, code-level exemption: scripts/check-slide-size.js line 68 hard-codes STORY_EXEMPT = new Set(['how-this-training-was-built', 'story-of-module-6']) with the comment 'Narrative lectures: read at home / told as a story, not squinted off a slide. Named exceptions per Antti.' Matches the maintainer block's own line 56, 'File is size-gate exempt (story lecture).' This is the tooled, permanent story-lecture category, not the ad-hoc file-level workaround the rule's prose warns against. Ran anyway with --include-stories --report to confirm no real overflow: chunk 1 186w/0b, chunk 2 154w/0b, chunk 4 (the new slide) 121w/4b, chunk 3 57w/0b — 'oversized: 0' even unexempted, well under 210 words / 6 bullets on every chunk including the new one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Three of four ## headings are unambiguous declarative claims (line 5 'Everything starts as a few bulletpoints somewhere', line 15 'Then we tested the training', line 25 'You just ran the same loop'). The new chunk 4 header 'What compounds' (line 31) is a topic-framing noun phrase rather than a subject-predicate assertion; the actual law ('each unit of engineering work should make subsequent units easier, not harder') sits in the body (line 33), not the header. Read against the rule's own carve-outs — catalogue entries naming their subject (Ralph, The numbers) are explicitly not violations, and the rule's own precedent (Antti 2026-08-15 on what-packaging-is.md, 'not every header owes a claim') licenses a topic-naming header where the definitional content follows in the body — the header stays inside: it accurately telegraphs the slide's topic to a reader scanning headers only, and the definitional claim itself is present on the slide (rule 6 is separately satisfied). Genuinely a close call because this IS the file's one law/consolidation slide, where the rule says the claim requirement binds hardest and the what-packaging-is precedent was an H1/title, not a ## heading — flagged as a rule_question rather than treated as settled.
